Interesting pattern with compute I keep seeing.  

So NVIDIA just used 8k GPUs to simulate a quantum computer that doesn't exist yet.  

The pattern is chips built for a specialized usecase solving problems better then general compute, and almost all one of them still needs GPUs to work.  

Everyone's heard of the inference chips, Groq, Etched, Cerebras, plus the hyperscalers' own, TPUs, Trainium, Maia.  As well as the large labs adding chips built for fast inference, but they still train their models on GPUs.  

And it's happening in every frontier field.

Massive AI debt = systemic crisis? Not so fast.

Blackstone’s Jas Khaira says the real story is different. It’s a financing gap — not a 2008-style banking meltdown.

Why that matters:

🔹 Blackstone’s playbook is compute-first. It launched Blackstone N1 in San Francisco and is deploying debt, equity and bespoke capital structures to fund data centers, neoclouds and chip plays.

🔹 Examples worth noting:
- CoreWeave: a $2.3B loan in 2023 against Nvidia GPUs and blue-chip customer contracts. That model scaled into follow-on debt.
- Crux AI: $5B commitment to commercialize Google TPUs via a neocloud partnership.
- Other deals: co-leading a $10B facility for Firmus and backing early chip startups

Blackstone’s Jas Khaira says fears over AI-buildout debt are overblown 

Private equity giant Blackstone is putting itself at the center of the AI boom, firm veteran Jas Khaira discussed last week on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt. 

It is writing checks via various strategies, ranging from offering massive loans to data centers to investing in frontier AI models and applications.

Earlier this year, the firm launched Blackstone N1 (BXN1), a San Francisco-based central hub for its AI initiatives. The group is led by Khaira, who relocated from New York to be at the epicenter of AI.
